name: desire for sex
description: Desire for the stimulation of the genital organ and associated brain chemicals.

guidance.description: Seeking sexual pleasure and validation is a major driver for many people. Its a basic primeval force that many cultures and people struggle to balance. There are more flavors of sex and sexuality than will be covered in the Experience Manual. You might consider finding reputable and mature sources of information.
If you struggle with addiction to the brain chemicals released during sexual activity to the point that it's causing problems for you or others, consider seeking reputable and mature sources of help.

Sex can compete with religion for dominance in influence over human behavior, so major religions have a lot to say about it. Because intercourse can cause real-world problems, it  may be worth considering what they have to say.

Scientists present different perspectives that may explain aspects of sexuality and the grip it has on us. Some of these perspectives are controversial, perhaps due to lack of correctness, or perhaps for cultural reasons. Deep waters.

variations.name: desire for validation sex
variations.description: A desire for sexual contact as evidence for being attractive enough to find a partner.
perceptions: Being sexually active means you're not ugly.

variations.name: peer pressure desire for sex
variations.description: A sense that being sexually active is a way of staying in the good graces of a social group.
perceptions: Being sexually active means you're cool.

commentaries.quote: Conflicting social norms can make any kind of sex complicated. It may help to understand where your own desire is coming from: social pressures, habits, escape, or biology.

There are many that consider sex a private matter that shouldn't be openly discussed because it might encourage young people. This is understandable, as the consequences can be significant. Not only is having a baby life changing, but you might not want to think about your grandparents in that way.
It is clear that sexual desire is one of the — if not the — strongest of human needs. Typically, it takes up a huge portion of our time, emotional energy, and lives.
Our failure to understand the real and paradoxical nature of human mating is costly, both scientifically and socially.
commentaries.attribution: David M. Buss in 'The Evolution of Desire'
